period.time_scale: UTC (ISO 8601, 'Z'); internally TDB seconds past J2000 via naif0012.tls

metrics.fraction_denominator: requested period (unknown time counts as not visible); *_of_known uses visible + not_visible time only

method.name: terrain-horizon visibility of Sun/Earth discs
method.sun_visible_definition: >= 50% of the solar disc above the terrain horizon
method.earth_visible_definition: >= 50% of the Earth disc above the terrain horizon
method.darkness_definition: < 50% of the solar disc above the terrain horizon (certain)

transition_refinement.note: numerical precision only; physical timing accuracy is limited by DEM resolution and may be minutes where the body grazes the horizon. Events shorter than the 240 s sampling step can be missed.

method.eclipse_handling: Sun eclipsed by Earth flagged per sample (geometric); not subtracted from sunlight

model.curvature: exact spherical geometry on the 1737.4 km sphere
model.radial_sampling: 40 m steps growing 0.3 %/step (1605 samples per ray)

near_field_dem.projection: south polar stereographic, lat_0=-90, k=1, R=1737400 m, x_0=y_0=0

far_field_dem.projection: south polar stereographic, lat_0=-90, k=1, R=1737400 m, x_0=y_0=0
far_field_dem.role: far field, COG overview level 1 (2x reduction of the 240 m/px raster, resampling method chosen by the data producer; summits can be smoothed)

dem.product: A New View of the Lunar South Pole from LOLA (PGDA product 90)
dem.reference: Barker, M. K., et al. (2023), Planetary Science Journal 4, 183, doi:10.3847/PSJ/acf3e1
dem.frame: MOON_ME of JPL DE421 (per product page)
dem.height_definition: surface height in metres above the 1 737 400 m reference sphere

ephemeris.aberration_correction: LT+S (light time and stellar aberration); observer at the site
ephemeris.body_frame_description: Lunar mean-Earth/polar-axis (ME) frame. Datasets are referenced to the ME frame of DE421; SPICE computations use MOON_ME as defined by moon_de440_250416.tf (alias of MOON_ME_DE440_ME421, the DE440 principal-axis orientation rotated to align with DE421 ME).

limitations: Prototype for site screening; not validated for flight operations and not NASA-approved.
Horizon from LOLA gridded DEMs (80 m/px within ~300 km of the pole, 480 m/px overview beyond): terrain smaller than the pixel scale (boulders, small crater rims, the lander itself) is not modelled.
The observer is a point at the stated height above the DEM surface at the stated coordinates.
Sun visibility is a geometric power *opportunity*; no power-system, thermal or array-pointing model.
Earth visibility is geometric line of sight to the Earth disc; no antenna, ground-station, link-budget or multipath analysis, so it does not prove a usable radio link.
Sun and Earth are uniform discs; solar limb darkening is ignored. Eclipses of the Sun by the Earth are flagged geometrically and not subtracted from sunlight.
Reachability, descent trajectory, navigation, slopes/hazards at lander scale and vehicle constraints are not evaluated.
